newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - March 28.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MARCH RISE LIFTS PRICES TO EIGHT-YEAR LANDMARK

Figures from the Nationwide Building Society show that house prices rose by nearly ten per cent in the year to March. This makes the month the best for prices since they peaked eight years ago. House prices have not shown a yearly fall for a year and have been rising by more than eight per cent for five consecutive months. The Halifax is to announce its house price figures for March next week and they are expected to show a less bullish view of the market.
-- REDLAND IN TALKS TO SELL LOSS-MAKING GRANULATS

Redland, the building material group, is in talks to sell its French aggregates business Granulats. The sale of France's largest aggregates operator represents a further dismantling of the Steetley business that Redland acquired for 670 million stg in 1992. Granulats is valued at 310 million stg in Redland's books and last year made a seven million stg loss. Robert Napier, Redland chief executive, said he was selling because weakness in the company's competitive position.
-- EUROPEAN PROTESTERS IN 'MARCH FOR JOBS'

Protestors are to stage a two-month march next month through 1,000 European towns, called "marches against unemployment, exclusion and precariousness". Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected to join the final rally on June 14, where EU heads of state are due to meet the following day to adopt a final text revising the Maastricht Treaty. Worker across Europe are growing increasingly fearful as austerity measures to bring their economies into line with the Maastricht criteria for economic union begin to take toll in terms of jobs.
THE TIMES
-- FLORIDA SUES P&O OVER COST OF PRINCESS CRUISES

Shipping and property conglomerate, P&O, has been accused of using unfair practices to lure customers on to its Princess Cruises liners in America and is now facing damages of one million dollars. The company will appear in court in Florida over allegations that it has pocketed a percentage of the surcharge that its advertisements bill as governmental-imposed "port charges" in order to make its cruises seem cheaper.
-- ORACLE'S ONE BILLION DOLLARS BID PLAN PUTS BITE ON APPLE

Founder of Oracle, Larry Ellison, is considering launching a bid worth more than one billion dollars for Apple Computer, the personal computer manufacturer. Ellison is proposing to oust the current Apple management, including chairman and chief executive. Ellison will join the board with Steven Jobs, the founder of Apple. The proposal may not be opposed by Gilbert Amelio, chief executive, whose pay package includes a ten million dollar severance fee.
-- OFTEL AIRS CONCERN ABOUT BT'S GROWTH

Telecommunications regulator Oftel has said it may impose restrictions on British Telecom to ensure that its overseas expansion plans are not funded at the expense of its core domestic operations. Oftel's director-general Don Cruickshank has said that it was possible moves towards globalisation by BT may have an impact on the company's ability and willingness to meet its UK licence obligations.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CHELTENHAM AND GLOUSESTER MEMBERS CASH IN AS TAXMAN CONCEDES

10,000 C&G customers are to receive tax rebates after the Inland Revenue accepted a decision on cash windfalls. The Inland Revenue did not appeal against a ruling by tax commissioners that said the cash bonuses paid to 800,000 C&G savers when the society was acquired by Lloyds Bank in 1995 should not be liable to capital gains tax. This means that C&G savers will receive the same tax treatment as customers of Alliance & Leicester, Halifax, Northern Rock and Woolwich.
-- CLAIMS OF RECORD GOLD FIND DEFENDED

Bre-X Minerals has been ordered to produce evidence that gold deposits worth 15 billion stg has been discovered at Busang in Indonesia. This comes after US group Freeport-McMoRan, a partner in the project, said its tests had shown an "insignificant" amount of gold at the site. Jakarta authorities has suspended Bre-X's mining licence and ordered the company to produce independent geological data.
-- TOP RAIL CHIEFS SACKED IN CULL BY NEW OWNERS

Senior industry sources claim that since the privatisation of rail passenger services, half of the chief executives of the 25 new train operating companies have been sacked or have left their jobs. All were experienced British Rail managers and 10 were the victims of failed management buy-out bids or were replaced after the new companies took over. However, others have been promoted by the new operators. Glenda Jackson, Labour's transport co-ordinator, said that rail privatisation had created "a cull of experienced rail managers".
THE INDEPENDENT
-- NEW MODELS AT CAR GIANTS TO SAVE 4,000 JOBS

Ford Motor Co and Peugeot have won the go-ahead to fund new models, thus securing 4,000 motor industry jobs on Merseyside and in the Midlands. The Government will give Ford a 15 million stg package of regional aid to build new vehicle at Halewood plant, much less than Ford had hoped for. Unions at Peugeot's Ryton plant in Coventry voted in favour of a two-year pay deal, paving the way for a 100 million stg investment.
-- MOTORING CLUBS REJECT TALK OF BID APPROACHES

The AA and RAC, two of Britain's leading motoring organisations, denied they had received takeover approaches from City financiers seeking to capitalise on an increase of bids for companies owned by their members. A spokesman for the AA said that it was aware that Andrew Regan's break-up approach to the Co-operative movement had prompted speculation about its ownership, but he said the company is committed to its present structure and strategy. Interflora also rejected similar reports.
-- MARKS AND SPENCER DENIES PLANS TO SELL BROOKS BROS

M&S has denied it is considering selling off its Brooks Brothers clothing stores in America. However, some City analysts say they regard the sale as inevitable. Nathan Cockrell, retail analyst at NatWest Securities, said that it was an open secret that M&S's chairman Richard Greenbury wanted to sell Brooks. A spokeswoman for M&S said she did not know where the rumours came from.
